brief: The canvas displays a dynamic, three-dimensional molecular model of the DNA double helix. Large, colored spheres representing the labeled nitrogenous bases (A, T, C, G) are arranged along a winding structural backbone. The central action is the dynamic interaction between the strands: temporary, distinct bonds form and break explicitly between complementary base pairs, illustrating the process of molecular pairing as the structure gracefully rotates and unwinds in space.

statement: This sketch renders a dynamic three-dimensional model of the DNA double helix using p5.js's WEBGL renderer. It visualizes the molecular structure with large, colored spheres representing nitrogenous bases (A, T, C, G) arranged in a helical backbone. The model rotates gracefully through space while showing temporary hydrogen bonds forming and breaking between complementary base pairs (A-T and C-G). The visualization demonstrates the dynamic nature of DNA pairing through a continuous animation that updates the positions of bases and their interactions over time, creating an organic, flowing representation of molecular behavior without any user input required.
